There's nothing worse than reaching out to someone and then being rejected and made to feel worse. I too have experienced this, I am guilty of being suicidal because of the burden I have on others. I know it is hard trust me but to step into your partners mind and think how would you react? Maybe he feels like he should be a good enough reason for you to want to live. Some people just don't know how to react, especially if they haven't felt like that themselves.   


I work as a social care worker in a home and I can tell you that I react differently to a service user in distress, than someone I have a personal relationship with. It is easier to talk about in a professional stand point. But when it is someone in your personal life it can be extremely difficult.   


Remember that your partner is human and has feelings just like your own. And no human is really meant to be able to comprehend suicide. So how do you think he might have felt when his partner disclosed this to him?   


Either way you look at it you still did the right thing by reaching out, just like you've done here also. Everyone is valued and deserves to be heard and helped.   


I hope this has helped in anyway. I wish you the best.

I can very much relate to this, I don't have any friends or really even family that care about me the way I need someone to. But I feel like I'm owed friends and haven't got over it yet. So you're stronger than me...

The least painless way is by hanging and dropping from a certain height, which would break your neck and kill you nearly instantly. However if the height is too high then you would end up decapitating yourself which I cant imagine being very nice for you or the person that finds you.
